steps.title: Prepare the base
steps.text: Heat the conventional oven to **177°C**. Mix **200 g GF digestive crumbs**, **67 g sugar** and **70 g melted butter**. The crumbs should be evenly damp and hold when pressed. If still loose, mix in the reserved **up to 15 g butter**, **5 g at a time**; stop before greasy or pasty. Record the amount used, discard unused melted butter.
steps.aside: This adjustment is our product-dependent proposal.

steps.title: Shape and prebake
steps.text: Press the crumb mixture across the ungreased 23 cm tin base and a little way up its sides. Compact evenly without crushing solid. Prebake **12–14 minutes**; look for a set surface and toasted-biscuit aroma. GF biscuit browning may differ. Leave on the rack while mixing the filling.

steps.title: Mix smoothly
steps.text: Beat **904 g Philadelphia cream cheese** with **200 g sugar** until smooth. Blend in **240 g sour cream**, **5 ml vanilla** and **10 ml lemon juice**. Add **3 eggs**, one at a time, stopping as each disappears. Scrape the bowl as needed; avoid whipping in air.

steps.title: Set up the bath
steps.text: Wrap the tin exterior in intact heavy-duty foil, bringing it well above the intended water line. Place in the roasting tin, add all the filling and smooth. On the oven shelf, carefully add just-boiled water around the wrapped tin to **about 2.5 cm depth**, keeping water out of the cake.

steps.title: Bake and cool
steps.text: Bake at **177°C** until the outside is set but the centre still gives a small wobble, about **55–70 minutes**. Check at the beginning of that range; stop baking when this cue is reached rather than waiting for the centre to become firm or for the full 70 minutes. Look for a cohesive central tremble, not liquid sloshing. The cake continues setting during its cooling and chilling stages. Tent loosely with foil if browning. Switch off, leave the door ajar and keep the cake in its bath for **1 hour**. Then remove the bath and outer foil and cool the tin on a rack; refrigerate once cooled. Follow the handling note below rather than leaving it out indefinitely.

steps.title: Chill and slice
steps.text: Cover and chill for **at least 4 hours**, preferably overnight. Loosen the edge and release the rim. For neat wedges, dip the knife into warm water and wipe it clean and dry between cuts. Slice only the number required; keep the rest chilled.

steps.title: Assemble the cheesecake
steps.text: For each of eight plates, place **1 slim slice**, spoon **20 g cold compote** towards the broad end, leaving the point and cut face visible, and finish with a little zest from **1 washed orange available**. Add **1 small pistachio shard** last, at the dry edge of the slice rather than submerged in compote. Taste the first plate before repeating the zest. Reserve **40 g compote and 2 shards** for two garnished spare portions, keeping sauce chilled and shards dry. Keep additional cake plain and refrigerated. The smaller compote batch is not intended to top every possible leftover slice.

items: Keep the cake untopped until serving. Sally supports making the plain cake up to **2 days** ahead, with **at least 4 hours** of chilling. Her slow-cooling method is retained; after the one-hour oven stage, cool on the rack promptly and refrigerate without an extended counter hold. Apply a maximum **2-hour counter-cooling window** after removal from the oven, refrigerating sooner once cooled; refrigerator **4°C**.

For this master, use refrigerated cake/leftovers within **2 days of baking**, a conservative project limit rather than Sally’s four-day leftover claim. Sally permits the plain cake to be wrapped in several film layers and foil and frozen for **up to 3 months**, thawed overnight in the fridge; confirm fully thawed before slicing. Freezing the GF base’s texture is untested. Never freeze with compote or shards attached.

recipes.title: Cranberry–orange compote
recipes.subtitle: For the cheesecake
batch: **Batch:** **half** the original source batch, to provide **10 garnished portions** alongside the full-size 23 cm cake. Additional cake is deliberately left plain; this batch does not promise to top every leftover slice. Actual finished mass/volume is **unmeasured**; the source half-yield is 1 US cup, not a gram conversion. Proposed allocation **20 g per portion = 200 g**, including **160 g for eight dinner plates + 40 g for two spares**. Measure the cold batch before portioning.

items: Use a medium saucepan, scales, spatula, citrus juicer/zester, clean spoon, shallow heatproof storage container and cold-water cooling bath. Rinse/sort **170 g fresh cranberries** (or use **170 g frozen cranberries**, without thawing, as Sally allows). Measure **90 ml water**, **30 ml orange juice**, **75 g light brown sugar** and **1/2 tsp finely grated orange zest** before heating. Avoid white pith.

rows.name: Cranberries
rows.amount: 170 g fresh or frozen, no dried fruit

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Put all **170 g cranberries**, **90 ml water**, **30 ml orange juice** and **75 g light brown sugar** into the saucepan. Stir over medium heat until the sugar dissolves and the fruit starts simmering.

steps.title: Cook gently
steps.text: Reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer. Stir periodically, letting the berries burst and the juices thicken. A full batch takes about **20 minutes total on the hob** (about **15 minutes after simmering**). Follow the cooled-spoon cue rather than halving the time. Crush remaining firm berries with the spatula for a softly textured, spoonable topping. Leave some berry pieces; do not boil down to a stiff jam. A cooled spoonful should settle softly, not stand as a firm lump.
steps.aside: This half batch may reduce sooner; its duration is **TBD**. All-fruit-at-start is our adaptation.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Remove from the heat and stir in the reserved **1/2 tsp orange zest**. The sauce thickens further as it cools. We omit vanilla here because the cake already supplies it.
steps.aside: Taste a cooled spoonful with a little cake if available before deciding any later revision to sugar; this master keeps the source’s fruit-to-sugar proportion.

steps.title: Cool and measure
steps.text: Transfer to a shallow container, cool promptly with a cold-water bath if useful, and refrigerate within **2 hours**. Once cold, weigh the compote and record yield. Stir gently before using. Reserve **200 g for 10 proposed 20 g servings**, with **160 g for eight dinner plates + 40 g for two spares**; keep the remainder separate and chilled. If too firm for the intended plate, revise consistency before adopting as a master rather than assuming a finished yield.

steps.title: Serve cold
steps.text: Use with the cheesecake; the single plating method and fresh orange finish are in that recipe. Never add warm compote to the chilled cake or put brittle into the stored sauce.

items: Keep covered at **4°C**, use within **2 days of preparation** under the conservative project leftover guidance. Sally’s original cranberry sauce allows five refrigerated days, but this fully cooked, vanilla-free adaptation does not claim that longer window. Make-ahead feasibility is supported; actual texture after chilling remains untested. For earlier preparation, Sally supports sauce freezing up to **3 months** and fridge thawing; use a labelled freezer-safe container with expansion space. Check the thawed consistency before plating.

recipes.title: Pistachio shards
recipes.subtitle: For the cheesecake
batch: **Batch:** **100 g sugar + 50 g pistachios + 0.5 g fine salt**, our proposed small batch. Finished mass, sheet area and intact shard yield are **TBD**; pan residue and breakage vary. Need **10 small, thin, intact shards**, eight for initial service plus two spare, plus spare fragments if the batch permits. One small shard per intended portion; the whole batch is not a ten-way serving allocation. Thickness target is visual, a single nut layer and translucent caramel between pieces, not a guaranteed measurement.

items: Set out a medium heavy, light-coloured frying pan; a large rimmed baking tray; **two sheets of baking parchment**; heatproof spatula; short rolling pin that fits inside the tray rim; oven gloves; dry airtight container. Ensure the parchment/tray can tolerate the chosen low oven setting. Clear a stable heatproof work surface.

Chop **50 g plain shelled pistachios** into small pieces, not powder. Measure **100 g caster sugar** and **0.5 g fine salt** (a scale capable of this amount is needed). Do not use salted nuts plus this full salt quantity without revising the formula.

Warm the parchment-lined tray and **50 g chopped pistachios** in a low conventional oven, proposed **100°C**, while setting up. Keep nuts warm, not browning. Remove with oven gloves only when ready to pour. Lay out the second parchment sheet and rolling pin first. All equipment must be dry.

rows.name: Plain shelled pistachios
rows.amount: 50 g, chopped into small pieces and warmed

notes: No fresh zest or juice goes into the caramel; the orange finish belongs to the cheesecake. This is a dry caramel, with no added water, syrup, butter or bicarbonate.

steps.title: Make caramel
steps.text: Spread **100 g caster sugar** across the dry pan. Heat moderately, tilting gently as it melts; avoid stirring the melting sugar. Let it become evenly amber. Allow about **4–5 minutes**, but watch the colour, not the clock. Do not let it smoke or become nearly black.

steps.title: Add nuts and salt
steps.text: Remove from the heat; stir in all **50 g warm chopped pistachios** and **0.5 g fine salt** quickly with the heatproof spatula. Coat evenly and immediately pour onto the warm lined tray. Do not pause to gather tools.

steps.title: Roll a thin sheet
steps.text: Spread briefly with the spatula, lay the second sheet of parchment over the hot mixture, and roll promptly from the centre outwards. Keep caramel away from the tray edge. Aim for one layer of small nut pieces and thin, translucent caramel gaps. Whole nuts/overlapping pieces prevent a delicate sheet. Use tools and oven gloves; never touch hot caramel through thin paper with bare fingers. Stop when it resists or starts cracking rather than forcing a setting slab.

steps.title: Cool and break
steps.text: Leave flat until fully cold and rigid. Remove the parchment, snap into small irregular shards, and select **10** with a delicate snap and green nut pieces visible. Record total yield and count of usable shards. Store extras separately; do not count them as plated portions.

steps.title: Finish at the pass
steps.text: Add **one small shard per plate**, last, following the cheesecake’s assembly. Keep it clear of wet compote as much as possible. Keep the other shards in their dry container while plating.

items: Once completely cold, store promptly in a **dry airtight container at room temperature**, separated by parchment. Do not refrigerate: condensation/humidity makes brittle sticky. Good Food supports airtight storage for its dry-caramel nut brittle; Celebration Generation supports a dry container and explains moisture sensitivity. [CHG-09/10]

For this untested thin adaptation, propose making it **no more than one day ahead for quality**, not as a tested shelf-life guarantee. Check a shard for a clean snap before service. Keep separate from cake/compote until plating. Do not use the refrigerator/freezer as a fix for soft caramel. If it has become sticky or bends, it is unsuitable for this garnish texture; do not promise it will recover. No longer storage window is assigned to this adapted formula.
